Reconstructed the same-interpreter failure from primary source: section 33 steps 1 to 8 are OS-level, step 9 (authorized-factory-consumer check) is the sole in-process Python-identity conjunct, implemented by _detect_caller_module / _verified_production_caller_name over module-level _PINNED_ dicts; failure mode F-A (recognition bypass via pin-state mutation / exec into module namespace / gc reach) and F-B (authority exfiltration -- even a perfectly recognized caller receives a Python authority object on a heap shared with attacker code). Enumerated a 15-entry threat model (T1..T15); inventoried the existing PCAE protected boundaries (HPAC-PAWA-001 section 4 filesystem trust root; HBDC-001 v1.2 standalone-admin-script precedent; HPAC-PPA-001 v1.0 out-of-process verified one-shot helper; scripts/hpac_certification_admin.py standalone consumer; the _PRODUCTION_WRITER_FACTORY_SEAL in-process primitive). Compared five candidate classes (6A persistent helper, 6B daemon, 6C short-lived one-shot privileged process, 6D HPAC-PPA-001 verified-helper reuse, 6E C-extension opaque handle) against a 20-criterion matrix. SELECTED: 6C -- a short-lived one-shot privileged helper process, realized as a generalization of the IV'd HPAC-PPA-001 verified-helper pattern (6D), anchored on the unchanged HPAC-PAWA-001 section 4 filesystem trust root, no second trust root: the standalone deployment-owner launcher integrity-verifies the out-of-band helper executable (byte hash / owner / mode / no-symlink / same-file-object exec), opens a private one-shot parent/child channel not inherited by agent code, exec's the helper; the helper runs the section 33 steps 1 to 8 OS recognition in its own interpreter (binding the configured-agent identity so the negative boundary keys off the agent principal not root under sudo), verifies its peer credential is the deployment owner, validates a narrow typed request bound to a certification session, performs exactly one bounded operation (a section 42 mutation / a five-role certification-lifecycle write / an enumerated section 42D read / one ceremony-entry hand-off to the presentation helper / one presentation-evidence write), writes audit evidence under the protected root, returns typed evidence only, and exits; no HPACWriterCapability / HPACStoreAuthority / handle ever crosses back to the main interpreter or the launcher; section 33 step 9 (calling module identity) is replaced by exec'd-from-the-verified-helper plus deployment-owner peer credential plus the OS recognition passing inside the helper. Adjudicated (phase-prompt section 8): the four-factory writer/factory-returns-a-capability abstraction is NO LONGER the correct production boundary -- the privileged side owns the mutation/read/ceremony-entry and exposes only typed protocol commands. Five-role certification family preserved exactly and mapped to five members of a closed operation enum with exact internal role dispatch; human approval / authentication / presence / PB permission / runtime capability / execution separation preserved; mechanism-neutral / mobile-only future path preserved; non-bearer / restart-dead semantics preserved and strengthened (properties of the process boundary rather than a fragile in-heap object); all section 5 / section 68 walls preserved. Defined the OS/process model, a narrow versioned one-shot protocol (HPAC-PAWA-HELPER/1.0 indicative), freshness/replay/failure semantics (explicit REQUEST RECEIVED -> AUTHENTICATED -> ADMITTED -> MUTATION STARTED -> COMMITTED -> EVIDENCE WRITTEN -> RESPONSE EMITTED transition model; response loss is never proof no mutation happened; no auto-retry), the packaging/deployment model, the macOS/Ubuntu cross-platform boundary (one logical contract, platform-specific peer-auth and launch backends), a migration plan (a compatibility shim MUST NOT preserve the insecure in-process authority path), nine recommended future implementation slices, an IV strategy, and the final-certification preconditions.
